text: The 2016 Prudential U.S. Figure Skating Championships took place from January 15 to 24 in Saint Paul, Minnesota, at the Xcel Energy Center and Bloomington Ice Garden. Medals were awarded in men's singles, ladies singles, pair skating, and ice dancing across senior, junior, novice, intermediate, and juvenile levels. These results contributed to the U.S. selection criteria for the 2016 Four Continents Championships, the 2016 World Junior Championships, and the 2016 World Championships. The host city was announced in November 2012. Competitors qualified through regional and sectional competitions held from October to November 2015. After these events, U.S. Figure Skating released a list of qualified skaters or those who earned a bye; skaters who later withdrew included Jason Brown, Jordan Moeller, Joshua Farris, Richard Dornbush, and Lydia Erdman / Alexey Shchepetov. Tarah Kayne / Daniel O'Shea won both segments to claim their first national title with a total score of 211.65 points, nearly 15 points ahead, while defending champions Alexa Scimeca / Chris Knierim earned silver with 196.80 points. Marissa Castelli / Mervin Tran placed third in both segments to win bronze, and Madeline Aaron / Max Settlage maintained their fourth-place position from the short program to earn pewter. Maia Shibutani / Alex Shibutani overcame a 0.47-point deficit in the short dance to defeat defending champions Madison Chock / Evan Bates and win their first senior national title. The team for the 2016 Winter Youth Olympics was announced in October 2015. The teams for the 2016 Four Continents Championships, the 2016 World Junior Championships, and the 2016 World Championships were all announced on January 24, 2016. Nathan Chen withdrew due to injury and was replaced by first alternate Tomoki Hiwatashi for the Four Continents and World Junior Championships, and by first alternate Grant Hochstein for the World Championships. On March 23, Polina Edmunds withdrew due to injury and was replaced by first alternate Mirai Nagasu.
